title: Kettles never shipped after a silent quality hold
brief: US retail customers report that SKU K-310 (kettle) has been out of stock at the Chicago DC since 3 Nov, two weeks earlier than planned. Find the root cause and an action plan.

evidence.content: US K-310 sell-out over the last 4 weeks was 6% above forecast, inside tolerance. No promotions.
Chicago K-310 on-hand 0 since 3 Nov. Replenishment PO 4471 (1,200 units) was due in on 27 Oct and has not been received; no ASN exists for it.
Hanoi Appliance confirmed PO 4471 on 2 Oct with ship date 6 Oct. The portal still shows status 'confirmed'.
There is no booking for PO 4471. The forwarder never received cargo-ready notice from Hanoi Appliance.

Supplier QA put lot K310-L9 (all 1,200 units of PO 4471) on hold on 4 Oct after a 3% thermostat failure rate at pre-shipment inspection. Rework is expected to finish 21 Nov. The buyer was not notified.
A cycle count at Chicago on 1 Nov matched the system for all kettle SKUs (no phantom stock).

answer_key.root_cause: The supplier put the whole PO 4471 lot on quality hold (thermostat failures) on 4 Oct and never told the buyer, so the replenishment never shipped while the portal still showed it as confirmed.

remediation_rubric.criterion: Get a firm rework date and ship good units early / partial shipment
Bridge the gap: transfer from another DC, air-freight part of the lot, or substitute SKU
Allocate scarce stock and tell customers revised dates
Require suppliers to notify quality holds; track confirmed POs against bookings/ASNs
Follow up on the thermostat quality root cause / inspection plan

answer_key.notes: E3 ('confirmed') is stale, not false. E6 rules out phantom stock.

registry.mechanism_opportunities: V2: Inventory may not realise the supplier QA detail matters. V3: E4/E5 contradict the 'confirmed' status in E3.
registry.favoritism_notes: Slightly favours protocols that let Supplier and Logistics findings meet quickly (V1).
